newsitem.title: THAILAND: U.S. First Lady lauds Thai anti-sex industry plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. First Lady lauds Thai anti-sex industry plan.

text.p: U.S. First Lady Hillary Clinton on Sunday praised a support programme in this northern Thai town aimed at keeping keeping young girls out of the sex industry.
Clinton made the comments in Chiang Rai, about 800 kms (480 miles) north of Bangkok in the Thai-Burma-Laos Golden Triangle region, soon after her arrival for a three-day visit to Thailand.

She visited the Thai Women of Tomorrow project in Chiang Rai -- one of the biggest markets for prostitute procurement. She also visited a hill tribe village where some of the villagers are beneficiaries of this programme.
"I am very impressed that families such as yours make the decision to send your daughters to school," Clinton said to a group of families seated outside a bamboo hut in the village near Chiang Rai.

"It is a wise choice and it will benefit both the family and the country," said Clinton, who was wearing a beaded necklace and holding a hand-embroidered hill tribe bag given to her as a gift from one of the awe-struck villagers.

The Thai Women for Tomorrow project was set up in 1992 and was partially supported by America's USAID. The programme is aimed at alleviating the child prostitution problem by giving young girls more educational and occupational opportunities.

Thousands of young girls are lured into the sex industry in Thailand every year, often with their parents being paid a sum of money by "agents" who then bring their daughters to big cities like Bangkok to work as bonded labourers in the sex industry, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) say.
About 10 percent of women forced into the sex industry are from the hill tribe area, an NGO worker said on Sunday.
Clinton had a brief conversation with girls involved in the project and their parents to discuss why they became involved. She asked one elderly lady why she decided to send her daughter to school.
"It is impossible in our current society not to have education," Ar Bea told Clinton through a translator.
"That is a wise decision. My husband, the President, and I also have a daughter. We believe she should be educated to make good decisions for herself in the future," said Clinton.
Clinton, also visited a girl's school in Chiang Rai upon her arrival from the Philippines mid-afternoon.
Clinton has made women's issues a focus of her two-day visit to two major northern Thai cities.
On Monday she will visit another project in Chiang Mai and give a speech at Chiang Mai University.

She will go to Bangkok late on Monday night to meet up with U.S. president Bill Clinton who arrives for a brief 27-hour visit to the Thai capital. It is the last leg of his first overseas trip since being re-elected earlier this month.
